title: 120/240 V split-phase utility service, 25 kVA transformer

sources.citation: A single-phase overhead (pole-mounted) distribution transformer serving a house: 25 kVA is a common size for one to a few homes, with an impedance of about 1.5–3 % and an X/R ratio of about 1–3, typical of published manufacturers' data and utility service guides for small single-phase units (paraphrased, not one vendor's). 2 % and an X/R of 2 are taken: a full-winding impedance of 0.02 × 240² / 25 000 = 46.1 mΩ, about 5.2 kA of bolted fault current across L1–L2, the infinite-primary (transformer-limited) available fault current: an upper bound, with no utility system impedance.
120 V from each line to the neutral (the secondary's centre tap), the 120/240 V single-phase three-wire nominal system of ANSI C84.1-2020 (the region profile's split-phase system).
game-design: a placeholder size and terminal layout. The service is headless in P2 (no service entrance or meter base until P4), so it is not drawn.

game-design: in P3 this service is the stand-in supply of the demo circuit (D12), standing in for P4's load centre, so each terminal takes one branch-circuit conductor: 14 to 10 AWG copper or aluminium, solid or stranded, a 13 ± 2 mm strip. The 4.0 N·m torque on all three is the breaker load terminal's value (breaker.saltmere-1p-15a), reused for simplicity; a real neutral bar is commonly marked lower (about 2.3 N·m, 20 lb·in, for 14 to 10 AWG), which P4's neutral bar will take. Conductors enter at the terminals and leave along +z. Not a transformer secondary's real terminals; P4 replaces it. Their contact and clamp values copy the breaker's screw class (ADR 0018 §8): a pressure plate gripping 10 mm, R₀ 0.3 mΩ (NBS BSS 103's good-connection class), a 0.026 W/K heat path and a 1.1 J/K clamp, all game-design here, like the torque.
game-design: the stand-in service terminals take the same slotted and square combination head as the branch breaker (the D12 stand-in for P4's load centre).
